close_reason: Doc-only fixes: updated stale/ambiguous rustdoc and CHANGELOG entries
description:
Scenario: two AIA HTTP adapter implementations diverge. Adapter A follows 3xx redirects internally and emits HttpStatus only for the final non-2xx response. Adapter B does not follow redirects and emits HttpStatus(301) for a redirect that adapter A would have followed.

Maintenance consequence: callers pattern-matching on AiaError::HttpStatus get adapter-dependent behavior with no contract to point at. The variant rustdoc at pkix-aia/src/lib.rs:124-134 says 'the remote endpoint responded with a non-success HTTP status. Carries the numeric status code (e.g. 404, 503).' It does not say whether HttpStatus(200) is constructible (logically wrong but type-allowed), whether 3xx is acceptable, or what happens with redirect chains.

Real-world relevance: CA/Browser Forum BR and Apple root program prohibit AIA URIs that redirect. An adapter conforming to either would surface HttpStatus(301/302) as the failure; an adapter following the more permissive RFC 5280 reading would surface HttpStatus(404) of the redirect target. These produce different cached results for the same upstream behavior, and a downstream policy layer matching on HttpStatus can't tell.

Fix: tighten the rustdoc on HttpStatus. State explicitly: the status code is the FINAL response status after the adapter's redirect policy has been applied; whether redirects are followed is adapter configuration. Adapters MUST NOT emit HttpStatus(2xx). Add a debug_assert in the doc that adapters should not emit success codes through this variant.

Pre-1.0 the variant could also be narrowed to non-2xx by construction via a newtype, but that is a bigger change.

Not a code defect today (no adapters exist yet — pkix-aia-http is separate). Filing because the contract solidifies before the first adapter ships.
title: AiaError::HttpStatus(u16) public contract ambiguous on 3xx/redirects/2xx
